title: Stability partner amplification plan (60d)
summary: Working plan to accelerate handoff and operational readiness across Platform, Serving Runtime, Product (Hosted API), and Solutions Engineering. Framed as a 60-day action canvas to amplify partner readiness and reduce first-call remediation for new model rollouts and capacity bursts. Emphasis on concrete cadence, lightweight runbooks, and metric-led canaries.
goals: Reduce on-call remediation time for model-serving incidents by 35% during first 30 days after rollout
Establish a repeatable partner onboarding checklist so feature teams can achieve SLO alignment within two sprints
Create three lightweight runbooks (canary, fallback to quantized variant, cross-region failover) and validate via tabletop
Define clear SLO acceptance criteria for hosted/dedicated/private model launches and automate gating in CI where possible
scope: Covers cross-team artifacts and activities required for operationalizing SLOs for model-serving features launched on Redwood Hosted and Dedicated. Excludes deep infra refactors and platform major releases; includes temporary mitigations (traffic shaping, model variant routing) and observability catchup tasks.
success_metrics: Mean time to detect (MTTD) for model-serving regressions drops from ~7m to <3m in measured experiments
Mean time to mitigate (MTTM) for severity-2 incidents reduces by 35% during pilot launches
90% of partner teams can complete onboarding checklist and pass SLO gating within 14 days
Canary pass rate target: >=95% for production-like workloads before full rollout
60_day_timeline:
Week 0: Alignment workshop (Platform, Serving, Product, Solutions). Agree KPIs, RACI, and minimal SLO definitions.
Week 1: Draft partner onboarding checklist; identify 3 partner teams for pilot. Create initial runbook templates (canary, model-fallback, capacity-escape hatch).
Week 2: Implement lightweight CI gate that runs smoke SLO checks against staging canary. Instrument synthetic traffic generator for p95/p99 latency tests.
Week 3: Tabletop exercise with partner teams: simulate prefix cache failure and model variant fallback. Capture gaps.
Week 4: Iterate runbooks and SLO acceptance criteria. Add alerting tags and playbook links to incident console.
Week 5-6: Pilot with partner team A (small-medium inference). Measure MTTD/MTTM, collect telemetry, run retrospective.
Week 7: Scale pilot to partner team B (bursty workloads). Test autoscaling and routing policies.
Week 8: Incorporate learnings, finalize runbooks, publish checklist in Drive + Confluence, and propose automation for gating in PR templates.
Milestone dates: Kickoff 2026-01-16, First tabletop 2026-01-30, Pilot A complete 2026-02-13, Publish artifacts 2026-02-27.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Observability gaps in token-level latency traces -> Mitigation: short-term add token_buckets sampling for critical endpoints and a synthetic load job that hits KV cache edge cases
Risk: Partner teams lack capacity to participate -> Mitigation: limit pilot to two teams and provide Solutions Engineering pairing hours (8h/week) for first 4 weeks
Risk: Canary failures are noisy and cause false positives -> Mitigation: tune canary thresholds, add short warmup and p95/p99 baselines from historical traffic
Risk: Rollout gating requires infra changes -> Mitigation: implement as optional CI step and use manual gating until infra tickets prioritized
decisions_needed: Approve minimal SLO set for pilot (Availability, p95 latency, p99 latency, error-rate on model outputs)
Confirm allocation of Solutions Eng time for pairing support (recommended 2 FTE-weeks total)
Agree on canary traffic volume (suggest 0.5%-2% of production traffic depending on model cost)

Miguel: provision synthetic load harness and baseline script (due 2026-01-22)
Hannah: author initial onboarding checklist doc and runbook templates (due 2026-01-25)

Lena: coordinate tabletop agenda and failure scenarios (due 2026-01-28)

runbook-summaries:
Canary runbook: deploy canary variant behind a routing policy, synthetic traffic + quick SLO assertions (availability, p95, p99), abort conditions and automated rollback to previous traffic weight.
Fallback runbook: route to quantized/lightweight model variant on high latency/error spike, escalate to on-call only if fallback fails.
Capacity escape hatch: pre-defined policy to throttle low-priority customers and divert traffic to Dedicated nodes in other region if autoscaling lag observed.
communication_plan: Weekly status email to stakeholders (Platform, Product, CS), dedicated Slack channel #stability-partner-amplify, rapid escalation path for severity>=2 incidents. Publish final artifacts in Confluence and link to partner onboarding checklist in PR templates.
open_questions: What exact thresholds should define a canary pass for generative text endpoints (p99 latency vs token-per-second tradeoffs)?
Do we have a standardized tag taxonomy for alerts so partner teams see combined context in the incident console?
Can Solutions Eng time be booked as a project budget or pulled from feature team capacity?
meeting_notes:
2026-01-16 Kickoff: agreed to minimal SLOs (Availability 99.9% for control plane, p95 latency targets region-specific). Decided to run 2 pilot teams. Action owners assigned.
2026-01-30 Tabletop: prefix cache eviction scenario exposed missing alert tag; Samir to prototype tag enrichment. Synthetic load found a p99 spike with padding tokens; Miguel to add KV-cache hot-key test.
Retros: partners want clearer rollback thresholds and a simple 'abort + notify' CI job. We agreed to add a dedicated checklist step in PR template.
notes_to_self: Keep artifacts lightweight — teams will adopt if friction low. Focus first on measurable improvements (MTTD/MTTM) rather than perfect SLO coverage. Capture three short videos walking through runbooks for partner teams.
